title: add cuda-graph capture/replay with shape-guards + warmup regression fix
author: Priya Singh
description:
Add end-to-end CUDA graph capture/replay support in the serving runtime with explicit shape guards and a deterministic warmup flow. Motivation: reduce kernel launch overhead for stable-shape request hot paths by capturing and replaying CUDA graphs while preserving correctness for variable-shape requests via lightweight shape guards. This PR also fixes a regression where warmup runs could record incorrect batch shapes leading to crashes during replay.

Changes include an opt-in GraphManager that groups identical operator shapes, a ShapeGuard layer that validates tensor dims before replay, and updated warmup: deterministic synthetic warmup sequences and a fallback re-capture path on guard mismatch. Also added metrics/tracing for graph hit/miss rates and a microbench harness for CI perf checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Graph capture/replay core implementation
- [x] ShapeGuard validation and mismatch handling
- [x] Deterministic warmup flow + re-capture fallback
- [x] Unit and integration tests (capture/replay, guard mismatch, KV cache compatibility)
- [x] Perf microbench and canary dashboard panels
- [x] Documentation and developer notes

Notes: The feature is behind a runtime flag (env var REDWOOD_USE_CUDA_GRAPH=true). Default remains off. We intentionally keep capture size conservative by capping sequence length and requiring KV cache affinity checks. See linked linear items for rollout plan and canary criteria.
